svg.title: Cleanout Gates Before Anything Leaves the House
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-cleanout-gate-tree; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Cleanout Gates Before Anything Leaves the House; subtitle: Secure, authorize, document and search before disposal; caption: Throw nothing away until a professional has looked; the market decides the value of the items, not the memories.; assumptions note: Gate order follows the shared sequence of probate realtors, haulers, liquidators and preservation contractors. Fee and return figures are attributed practitioner claims.; note: Gates per JunkRemovalWeb, Gyd Path, Local Probate Help, Cesar Espinoza, Illinois Probate Solutions, BizMove, At Home with Jody, Smile Abroad, and JM Junk Removers.; nodes: gate: G1; question: Has the person with legal authority signed before a single item is loaded?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop. Nobody loads a truck until that person signs; where two heirs inherit, get both signatures.; gate: G2; question: Is every room, garage, shed and closet photographed or on video?; pass next: G3; fail action: Shoot the preliminary inventory before any contents move.; gate: G3; question: Have books, coat pockets, high shelves, tins and shoeboxes been searched?; pass next: G4; fail action: Run the one-pass search; one hoarder-home sort turned up $5,000 in jewelry and nearly $30,000 in cash.; gate: G4; question: Has a professional looked at valuable or unique items?; pass next: Choose the sale route: DIY ($400 in expenses turned into well over $10,000) or a company (base minimum plus 25-50% or more), then quote cleanout as load price plus labor.; fail action: Hire an appraiser for valuable or unique items before disposal.

text.title: Cleanout Gates Before Anything Leaves the House
text.tspan: Cleanout Gates Before Anything Leaves the House

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Has the person with legal authority signed before a single item is loaded?; pass next: G2; fail action: Stop. Nobody loads a truck until that person signs; where two heirs inherit, get both signatures.
gate: G2; question: Is every room, garage, shed and closet photographed or on video?; pass next: G3; fail action: Shoot the preliminary inventory before any contents move.

gate: G3; question: Have books, coat pockets, high shelves, tins and shoeboxes been searched?; pass next: G4; fail action: Run the one-pass search; one hoarder-home sort turned up $5,000 in jewelry and nearly $30,000 in cash.

gate: G4; question: Has a professional looked at valuable or unique items?; pass next: Choose the sale route: DIY ($400 in expenses turned into well over $10,000) or a company (base minimum plus 25-50% or more), then quote cleanout as load price plus labor.; fail action: Hire an appraiser for valuable or unique items before disposal.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order follows the shared sequence of probate realtors, haulers, liquidators and preservation contractors. Fee and return figures are attributed practitioner claims.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order follows the shared sequence of probate realtors, haulers, liquidators and preservation contractors. Fee and
return figures are attributed practitioner claims.
